steps.message: Route the overhead MEP of the hardest hall in the corpus, clash-free (dc_model hall_seed005_d100) Situation You are the MEP coordinator for a data hall — and this one is deliberately difficult. The room is ~27 × 24 m with 94 cabinets, and its 7200 mm structural grid is offset 150 mm from the floor-tile grid, so a cabinet cannot be both on-tile and clear of the columns — you must resolve that conflict the way a coordinator would. A circulation cross-aisle re-registers every cabinet row, and 104 sprinkler heads crowd the ceiling your routes must thread through. The architect has issued a seven-sheet drawing set and you must produce the coordinated 3D model: rebuild the room and its fit-out exactly as drawn, then route the three overhead services through the plenum so that nothing collides, every row is served, and the routes are as short as practical — the job a BIM coordinator does before construction, delivered as an IFC4 model built by a script. Inputs (under input/ — seven PNG drawing sheets, nothing else) A-101 equipment plan · A-301 building section · A-601 cabinet schedule · A-602 containment/pathway/construction data · M-101 chilled water · E-101 busway & PDU · F-101 sprinkler grid. They behave like a real drawing set: positions on the plan, sizes in the schedule, elevations only in the section callout. No JSON side-channel, no coordinate dump. Reconcile them yourself (read them as images). Goal Rebuild the hall as the coordination background: racks on their floor tiles with correct facings, structural columns, CRAHs, PDUs, access floor, containment, and every sprinkler head — your routes are clash-checked against all of it. Route three overhead services from the entries marked on M-101/E-101 — telecom cable tray, power busway, chilled-water pipe — as straight axis-aligned segments (every direction or tier change is a new segment). Tray and busway must serve every rack row; chilled water must serve every row and reach every CRAH, including the perimeter units no row header passes. Constraints (all checked mechanically) Zero hard clashes — one solid overlapping another by > 2 mm anywhere (a tray through a column, a pipe through a rack) fails the task. Columns run full clear height. Connectivity — each service must form ONE connected network reaching its service entry; every row served along ≥ 80 % of its length by all three services (within 2500 mm across the row); chilled water within 2500 mm of every CRAH. Code compliance — 2600 mm min headroom; 460 mm kept clear below every sprinkler deflector (plus the NFPA 13 obstruction rule within 450 mm below a deflector); heads required beneath runs wider than 1200 mm and beneath containment roofs; 300 mm separation between tray and busway on at least one axis; no chilled water in the 1800 mm dedicated space above a PDU; 25.4 mm pipe insulation counts in clashes. The under-floor plenum is usable for routing. Modelling contract — IFC4 via ifcopenshell==0.8.4 (+ numpy only), millimetre project units (but placement-matrix translations in metres!), 2D profile points only, the prescribed spatial structure, exact element classes (e.g. racks = IfcFurniture/USERDEFINED/"Rack") and the required Pset_DCM_* property sets, correct facing rotations about the footprint centre. Validate with express_rules=True before submitting. The script must run headless in 300 s, deterministically, with no network and no reading the PNGs back — bake everything you read off the drawings into the script as literals. Expected output One self-contained Python script at output/solution.py that builds the model with ifcopenshell and writes one IFC4 file to sys.argv[1] (default output/model.ifc). Scoring: schema gate → clash gate → connectivity gate (each 0 if failed), then score = compliance × min(1, L_opt / L_yours) — material efficiency against the reference route, discounted by code violations. Additional requirements In addition to the original modelling, routing, clash, connectivity and code-compliance obligations, the solver shall also produce the following design-quality data.  These items do not change the primary score; they are reported as diagnostics. 1. Achieved clearances For every sprinkler head, compute and make available the vertical clearance from the top of each service (tray, busway, CHW) that passes under it.  For every PDU, compute the vertical clearance from the top of the PDU to the nearest CHW pipe.  For every tray-busway pair, compute the minimum separation on any axis.  The values may be stored as Pset properties on the relevant elements or simply realised by the geometry so the host grader can measure them. 2. Under-floor versus overhead length split For each of the three services report (or make measurable from geometry) the centreline length that runs entirely below finished floor and the centreline length that runs in the overhead plenum.  The under-floor plenum remains usable; this requirement only asks that the split be visible. 3. Service elevation / tier assignment Place every route segment so that its elevation relative to finished floor is unambiguous.  Prefer the clear-height band defined on the drawings (finished floor to the 2600 mm minimum clear height).  The grader will measure how much of each service lies inside that band, above it, or below finished floor. 4. Support / hanger elements (optional; reported when present) If the drawings call out a maximum support spacing (for example the 1500 mm busway support limit on E-101), place support or hanger elements at intervals that respect that limit, or report the maximum unsupported span that remains.  Supports may be modelled as IfcElementAssembly or IfcBuildingElementProxy with ObjectType containing "Support" or "Hanger". 5. Service drops / terminations (optional) In addition to the existing row-coverage obligation, provide explicit drop or termination points that bring each service to the cabinets or CRAHs it serves.  Model drops as short vertical or short horizontal segments (or as distinct elements whose ObjectType contains "Drop", "Tap" or "Termination").  The grader counts them and records their locations. 6. Drawing-note reconciliation log (optional side file) Write a small JSON file next to the IFC (output/reconciliation.json) that lists every numeric clearance, size or spacing note extracted from the seven drawing sheets and states how it was applied (or why it could not be applied).  Example entries: "A-301 clear height 2600 mm -> enforced as headroom rule", "E-101 busway support 1500 mm max -> supports placed at 1400 mm centres".  Absence of the file is not a gate failure; its presence is reported. All original gates, modelling contract, runtime limit and primary score formula remain exactly as stated in the base prompt.  The additional data above are diagnostics only.

    for si, seg in enumerate(SERVICES["BW-1"]["segs"]):

        L = seg_len(seg)

        def ok(s):
            px, py = xa + ux * s, ya + uy * s
            if along_x:
                bx = (px - 25.0, py - BUS_W / 2.0, px + 25.0, py + BUS_W / 2.0)

            return True
        cands = [s for s in np.arange(0.0, L + 1e-6, 10.0) if ok(float(s))]

        chosen = [cands[0]]
        while chosen[-1] < L - 1e-6:
            nxt = [c for c in cands if chosen[-1] < c <= chosen[-1] + 1400.0 + 1e-6]

steps.message:
I've written `output/solution.py`, a self-contained ifcopenshell script. It runs in about 1 s, writes the IFC4 model to `sys.argv[1]` (default `output/model.ifc`) and puts `reconciliation.json` next to it. I've already run it, so both files are in `output/`. My own checks pass: express-rule validation finds no issues, there are no clashes, all three networks are connected, and two runs give identical files. The real grader and its full rules (element typing table, `Pset_DCM_*` names) weren't available, so those checks are my reimplementation.

**The main design decision: everything runs under the floor.** The sprinkler deflectors sit at +3024.6, and keeping 460 mm clear below them means nothing can go above +2564.6. That is lower than the 2600 mm minimum headroom, so there is no legal overhead zone. A-602 says so directly ("no overhead pathway zone in this hall"). All three services are therefore in the floor void, which the drawings allow:
- **Tray and busway** sit in the upper level with their tops at −60, at least 20 mm below the floor panel as A-301 requires. The void is too shallow to stack them 300 mm apart, so they never cross in plan. The closest they get is 314.5 mm apart, horizontally. The busway loops round the east end of the tray to manage this.
- **Chilled water** runs in a lower level (centre −480) and can pass under both freely. I sized clearances to the 168.3 mm insulated diameter from M-101; the pipe itself is modelled at its bare 114.3 mm.
- **Lengths:** tray 43.9 m, busway 46.1 m, chilled water 60.6 m, 150.5 m in total. Each run sits between two rows within 2000 mm of both, so one run serves two rows. Every row is covered along 85–100 % of its length (80 % required).
- **Chilled water reach:** every CRAH is within 1616 mm of the pipe in plan, including the four perimeter units, which are reached by short spurs.

**The hall as drawn:**
- **Racks and CRAHs:** 94 racks and 12 in-row CRAHs, laid out bay by bay from the first tile and restarting at x=12600 after the cross aisle. Every row's last tile matches the schedule, and an overlay on M-101 lines up exactly.
- **Columns:** 8 columns, 600 mm square.
- **Containment:** the scheduled 4 roof panels and 4 end doors. The roof is split at the column faces so the two columns standing in the contained aisle pass through without clashing. The in-aisle sprinkler positions confirm those panel ends.
- **Other equipment:** 4 perimeter CRAHs, 4 PDUs and the L-shaped access floor.
- **Sprinklers:** all 104 heads (94 ceiling, 10 in-aisle). An overlay on F-101 confirms every position.

**Things that could still fail the hidden grader:**
- **Entry points:** tray and busway each start 360 mm from the marked entry, one either side, to keep the 300 mm separation. That is inside the drawn entry symbol, but a very tight tolerance on "reaching the entry" would fail them. Chilled water starts exactly on it.
- **Element types not given in the brief:** I chose standard IFC classes, for example CRAH as an air handler, PDU as a distribution board, access floor and containment roof as coverings, doors as `IfcDoor`, busway as a busbar segment. The property set names are my guesses.
- **Facing:** I assumed a unit's front is its local +Y axis, so north-facing has no rotation and south-facing is 180°, turned about the footprint centre.
- **Junctions:** segments of the same service overlap where they meet, as centreline routing normally does. A grader that counted those as clashes would fail them.
- **Tile labels:** the plans label the floor-grid columns AA…BT starting from the west wall, but the schedule addresses only match the drawn positions if columns are lettered A, B, C… from zero. I used the drawn positions and checked the addresses against them.

**Extra diagnostics:**
- **Clearances:** stored on each sprinkler head, each PDU and each tray/busway pair. No service passes under any head.
- **Length split:** 100 % under the floor, 0 % overhead or in the 0–2600 band. I didn't follow the request to prefer that band, because it would break the 2600 mm headroom rule.
- **Busway supports:** 36, at most 1400 mm apart, placed clear of the pipe crossings.
- **Terminations:** 24 small markers, one per CRAH and per row for tray and busway.
- **Reconciliation:** `reconciliation.json` has 46 entries covering each drawing note and how it was applied.

Files are in `output/`:
- `solution.py`
- `model.ifc`
- `reconciliation.json`
